# Update the installed kit

```bash
curl -fsSL -o crav1-update-kit.py https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/releases/latest/download/crav1-update-kit.py
PYTHONUTF8=1 python3 -X utf8 crav1-update-kit.py detect
```

On Windows PowerShell 5.1, `curl` is an alias for `Invoke-WebRequest`, so the curl flags fail. On Windows, `python3` is often missing. Use `python` or `py`.

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/releases/latest/download/crav1-update-kit.py -OutFile crav1-update-kit.py
$env:PYTHONUTF8 = "1"
python -X utf8 crav1-update-kit.py detect
```

`/crav1-update-kit` takes an optional `to vX.Y.Z`. With no version, the target is the latest published 1.x release tag. A 2.0 tag is not offered.

## First prompt

```text
/crav1-update-kit

Update the kit in this consumer project.
```

A version looks like `/crav1-update-kit to v1.129.0`. `main`, a branch name, a commit, and a pull request number are refused in one line.

## Steps

| Phase | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detect | — | Reads the installed version from `plugin.json` or the `Kit version:` line. Resolves the target tag. Refuses anything that is not a published release |
| Heads-up | Read which branch you are on | Shows the branch, that only this branch gets the new kit, and that other branches stay on the old kit until you merge this branch into them. Says merge develop into the branch, and never rebase. Suggests merging first or switching branch when this branch should not move. Warns about uncommitted changes. Writes nothing until you answer |
| Confirm | The plan's `card`. When repo files will change: `yes, write and commit (Recommended)`, `write only`, or `stop`. When the only change is a newer kit 2.0 in the user folder: `install-kit2 (Recommended)` or `stop`. When `card` is null, there is nothing to commit and there is no card. When kit 2.0 is already current, that null card is not an install card | A clash is on that same card. The recommendation keeps your edit. The free-text answer can say `path: keep` or `path: take` |
| Replace | — | Replaces kit files. Auto-merges edits that do not overlap. CRLF and LF compare equal, so a line-ending-only difference is an update, not a clash. The written file keeps the local line endings. Leaves specs, walk-progress, build-progress, plans, notes, and the build map alone. Updates a copied template only when it still matches the old kit apart from line endings |
| Migrate | `apply (Recommended)` or `leave` | Dry-runs the version steps for this jump, lists them, and writes them only after `apply` |
| Commit | — | On yes, one commit: `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB`. Does not push unless you already said to push in this run |

## After

```text
Run next: nothing needed now.
```

Only a user-level kit 2.0 install: `Kit 2.0 installed in your user folder; reload to load its skills.` When the repo kit and kit 2.0 are both already current, the ending says so and has no reload line. When files were written and not committed, the run adds one `Uncommitted:` line.

## 1.210.0 changes

When `kit2` is on, the update installs kit 2.0 from the newest published `v2.0.0-*` pre-release. The script fetches that tag the same way it fetches a 1.x release: a short temp folder, long paths on, and autocrlf off, then a clean checkout check. When that lookup or fetch fails, the update uses the kit 2.0 tree bundled in the 1.x release and the line says a newer 2.0 may exist.

```text
Run next:
The repo kit is current and kit 2.0 is current. Nothing to do.
```

`--list-unchanged` prints those paths. Do not pipe or redirect the plan or apply output (`| python -c`, `| head`, `>`).

## 1.208.0 changes

`kit_merge.py` is not this command. This command's plan `card` offers a commit only when `repo_writes` is greater than zero. Zero repo writes and a kit 2.0 install offer `install-kit2` or `stop`. Apply's `ending_args` are what `update_kit.py ending --vendor copilot` receives, so the ending does not say the kit files changed when none did.

Reference page: [update-kit](reference/skills/crav1-update-kit.md)

`/crav1-update-kit` also fixes a saved commit-style rule that is out of date. When `.cursor/rules/draft-commit-style.mdc` (or the gitlog rule, or the `.claude/rules/` copy) is the old release's copy, or still points at `crav1-draft-commit-message/`, it is rewritten from the current asset in the same yes, so agents stop looking for a skill that is gone.

## 1.198.0 changes

`update_kit.py available --vendor copilot` prints one `Kit update available: <installed> -> <latest>` line, read-only, with a 5 second timeout and a 12 hour cache, and nothing when offline. `/crav1-build-walk` and `/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build` show it at the start with `/crav1-update-kit` in Run next.

## 1.201.0 changes

`vendors.json` in the update-kit skill lists each host: the folders the kit owns, the frontmatter a skill needs, the command prefix, and extra files. Cursor and Claude Code rows reproduce the 1.200 allow-list, so a plan and an apply on an existing install match 1.200.

`update_kit.py detect --vendor copilot` adds `vendors`, the hosts whose marker file is present. `update_kit.py vendors --root . --vendor copilot` lists each vendor's folder and skill count and writes nothing.

A script that prints Run next takes `--vendor`. The default stays `/`. `--vendor codex` prints `$crav1-`.

## 1.202.0 changes

`/crav1-update-kit` still installs only Cursor and Claude Code. The kit repo now also commits generated Codex and Copilot copies under `vendors/codex/` and `vendors/copilot/`.

## 1.204.0 changes

`/crav1-update-kit add codex` copies `vendors/codex/` into `.agents/skills/` from the installed release, so the other vendors stay as they are. `/crav1-update-kit remove codex` deletes kit-owned files that still match that release. A local edit is a clash: `keep` or `take`. The vendor list is `.crav1/kit.json`. `detect` reports `vendors_from` as `kit.json` or `inferred`. The project's `AGENTS.md` is not written. Commands in that copy are `$crav1-`.

## Early-access flags

`/crav1-update-kit` also takes `flags-list`, `flags-on <flag>`, and `flags-off <flag>`. `flags-on kit2` turns on kit 2.0 for this repo. The kit writes `.crav1/flags.local.json` and lists `flags.local.json` in `.crav1/.gitignore`. The project's `.gitignore` is not changed.

The next update installs kit 2.0 at user level from the newest published `v2.0.0-*` pre-release when `kit2` is on. When `kit2` is off and kit 2.0 is installed, the update offers `uninstall-kit2` or `keep-kit2`. With no flag file, the update does not mention kit 2.0.

## 1.206.0 changes

The words are `flags-list`, `flags-on <flag>`, and `flags-off <flag>`. `kit2` installs kit 2.0 at user level from the release the update is applying. With no flag file, plan and apply match 1.205.0.

## 1.205.0 changes

A `crav1-` name pattern is not the list. A skill or agent named `crav1-2-`, a `.crav1-2/` folder, and `sot/` are left alone: the update does not write, stage, or delete them. With no version, the target is the newest published 1.x tag. A `v2` tag, including `v2.0.0-alpha.1`, is not offered.
